description: The fabric's own hygiene list, applied to every slice, skill and prompt section in every project, beside the credential and language checks in tools/fabric/layout.py and each project's .agent-fabric/hygiene.json. A person is named by role, never by name — the CEO, the owner, an agent by its login: a distilled slice travels into every project's repository and a name in it is a privacy matter, not a style one (decided 2026-09-16). refer_as says what the corpus says instead. A GitHub owner is named only if it is an organization on the owner list that the four GitHub patterns share (a personal handle is a privacy matter like a name); Written by fabric-coordinator.

patterns.label: an account or handle built from a person's name (a GitHub login, a Claude account, a key's variable) -- name it by whose it is
person's name -- refer to the CEO by role
private-network address (10.0.0.0/8) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
private-network address (192.168.0.0/16) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
private-network address (172.16.0.0/12) -- say 'a private address' or name the role
a /home/<login>/ path -- write the path from the repository root or ~/
host scratch path -- name the artifact by commit, sha and how to rebuild it; a path on one host's volatile volume is gone after a wipe and means nothing elsewhere
one account's scratch path -- name the artifact by commit, sha and how to rebuild it
a GitHub URL under an owner that is no listed organization -- name the repository by its project id; a personal handle is a privacy matter, an organization is added to this pattern's owner list
an <owner>/<repo>#N reference under an owner that is no listed organization -- name the project by its id; an organization is added to the owner list of the GitHub URL pattern
a repos/ path or --repo/-R argument under an owner that is no listed organization -- use <owner>/<repo> or the project id; an organization is added to the owner list of the GitHub URL pattern

a repository named <owner>/<repo> after repo or repository, under an owner that is no listed organization -- name the project by its id; an organization is added to the owner list of the GitHub URL pattern
